🚨🇲🇽 <u>THE 'SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS' — AND THE TWO COUNTRIES THAT WON'T SALUTE</u>

Contralínea maps Washington's new hemispheric military bloc, launched in Miami on March 7 with Rubio, Hegseth and Bessent and signed by a dozen governments from Argentina to Panama. Two names are missing: Mexico and Brazil — "the two principal countries that presently constrain absolute US hegemony over Latin America." The pitch is security; the product is access to oil, lithium, minerals and water, with every left government pre-labeled "narco-terrorist."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO PIVOTS TO EUROPE — MOCTEZUMA CONFIRMED AS EU AMBASSADOR</u>

The same envoy who ran Mexico's embassy in Washington until June is now headed to Brussels: the Permanent Commission ratified Esteban Moctezuma as ambassador to the EU, Belgium and Luxembourg, 28 votes to 8. The timing isn't subtle — it follows May's modernized Mexico-EU Global Agreement, and it lands as trade diversification away from Washington stops being a talking point and becomes personnel.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO US TREASURY: SHOW THE PROOF OR DROP THE SMEAR</u>

Washington's Treasury sanctioned 11 Mexicans and companies over a fuel-theft ("huachicol fiscal") network — then claimed the money financed political campaigns in Mexico. Sheinbaum's answer: "We were never informed of that. What proof do they have? It's the same as always: saying something happens without any evidence." The named suspects were already under Mexican UIF investigation — Washington just jumped ahead of the joint work to bolt on an unsubstantiated campaign-financing line.

🐉🇲🇽

The first Chinese automaker to build cars in Mexico arrives — just as the T-MEC targets "Chinese content"

GAC will become the first Chinese OEM to operate an assembly plant in Mexico, with production starting in the second half of 2026. It's a flexible line able to build combustion, hybrid, plug-in and electric models — the EMZOOM, AION UT and the coming GS7 — part of the company's "One GAC 2.0" strategy to localize production instead of just exporting into the market.

The timing is everything. Chinese FDI into Mexico fell roughly 80% in 2025 as firms waited for regulatory clarity. GAC's answer is to plant roots: local development, local jobs, proximity to the consumer — exactly the value-added the T-MEC review claims to want, but built with Chinese capital.

That's the sovereignty test in one factory. Washington frames Chinese investment as infiltration; Mexico can frame it as leverage — production, technology and employment on Mexican soil, on Mexican terms. Diversification isn't choosing Beijing over Washington. It's refusing to let either one write the rules alone. 🌐

🇲🇽🐉🔥

Mexico's T-MEC review opens today — and China sits at the table without a chair

The first joint review of the USMCA/T-MEC formally begins July 1. China won't send a negotiator, yet Washington has turned the whole process into a China question: can Mexico keep serving as North America's factory floor without becoming a "side door" for Chinese goods, parts and capital? The pressure is to tighten rules of origin and bolt on China-specific content limits.

Mexico isn't waiting to be told what to do. On January 1 it imposed duties of up to 50% — the WTO ceiling — on Chinese cars, steel and auto parts, and Ebrard is working the U.S. demands on Mexico's own timeline. The consistent line: consolidate the tariff advantage inside North America while refusing to slam any door in Asia.

The sovereignty point is simple. Rules written to fence out "Chinese content" don't stop at China — they catch the whole web of Asian suppliers North American factories already depend on. Mexico's task in this review is not to fight Washington's fight, but to make sure the terms get written in Mexico City too. 🌐

🇲🇽✊ 26,000 homes delivered. Housing is a right, not merchandise. "We're going to hold a 'Housing Wednesday.'" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, launching a weekly housing link Over 26,000 homes have been delivered across 98 developments under the Housing for Wellbeing program. The first weekly link went to Ahome, Sinaloa, where 96 families received keys. One beneficiary: a two-bedroom apartment, and no more rent.

🇲🇽🌎 The treaty doesn't die today. No panic. "If the US doesn't decide to extend for 16 years today, the treaty stays in force for the next 10 years — its full term, until 2036. It's not that the treaty ends; the 10 years continue, with reviews." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the USMCA (T-MEC) review June 30 was the deadline for a joint 16-year extension. Mexico and Canada signed; the US didn't. Under Article 34.7, the deal runs to 2036 regardless, with annual reviews. Mexico is also opening other trade agreements.

🇲🇽🌎 "An embassy is like a small piece of your territory." "An embassy is like a small piece of [our] territory." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on relations with Ecuador In April 2024 Ecuadorian police stormed Mexico's embassy in Quito to seize a former vice president who had been granted asylum — a breach of the Vienna Convention. Mexico cut ties. Asked about restoring them, Sheinbaum was open to dialogue but firm on the principle Ecuador broke.
